_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.

themes.title: Section 338 Canada tariffs — Aug 19 deadline postponed to Aug 21, 'substantial progress' cited, extended-negotiation phase, retaliation cliff still live
themes.summary: The Section 338 binary did not resolve cleanly at 12:01am ET on August 19. On August 18, Prime Minister Carney's office released a statement confirming that the United States has agreed to postpone implementation of the 50% Section 338 tariff until end-of-day August 21. The statement cited 'substantial progress' in negotiations but acknowledged that 'there is important work still to be done.' This is scenario (2) from prior framing — a partial delay that prevents an immediate market gap but does not retire the theme. It signals that a deal is closer than the 'stalled' characterisation from Benzinga (Aug 16) and the 'not satisfied' read from CBC (Aug 12-13) implied, but is not concluded. The new hard deadline is August 21 end-of-day — 48 hours from now. The statutory mechanics remain unchanged: a 50% additional ad valorem tariff on approximately $20 billion of Canadian goods (motor vehicles, dairy, alcoholic beverages, cement, furniture, fishing rods, seeds, clothing, hockey sticks) would stack on top of all existing duties with no USMCA exemption. Energy, potash, fish, critical minerals, and Section 232-covered goods (steel, aluminum, autos/parts already under 232) remain excluded. The postponement is a meaningful de-escalation signal relative to the prior 'stalled' framing, but the Aug 21 deadline re-creates binary risk in 48 hours. USDCAD should partially retrace the tariff-risk premium on the open Aug 19, but will not fully rally to deal-struck levels until a deal is confirmed. The Charette 'cliff' and 'nothing holds anymore' retaliation warning remains the Canada-side stated policy if tariffs eventually land. Section 338(b) escalation to a full import ban remains the statutory tail risk if Canada retaliates and the US deems it discriminatory escalation. The gap under negotiation per prior reporting centred on the depth of US tariff rollbacks on Section 232 steel/aluminum/autos/lumber versus Canada's retaliatory tariffs — the 'substantial progress' language suggests the gap has narrowed materially.

implications.CAD: PARTIAL relief on Aug 19 open — the postponement to Aug 21 reduces gap-up risk that was priced into USDCAD going into the deadline. However, the new Aug 21 end-of-day binary recreates two-sided risk: (1) Deal struck by Aug 21 = sharp CAD relief 100-150 pips from pre-Aug 19 levels, retire theme — now the elevated-probability path given 'substantial progress' language; (2) Tariffs land Aug 21 = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, Canada retaliation cliff materialises, theme intensifies. Do not carry unhedged CAD exposure into Aug 21 close. The 'substantial progress' framing makes a deal more likely than not by Aug 21, but not certain.
implications.USD: USDCAD is the dominant near-term directional driver for the pair; the Aug 21 binary supersedes Fed/Jackson Hole narrative for USDCAD specifically over the next 48 hours. Broad USD softness from data miss trifecta (NFP + CPI + PPI) is a secondary counterweight. FOMC minutes today (Aug 19, 2pm ET) are the primary near-term USD directional catalyst outside the Canada track.
implications.MXN: Secondary exposure — USDMXN can telegraph risk sentiment around Canada shock in real time. US-Mexico USMCA track advancing more smoothly per prior reporting.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD may be volatile around Aug 21 resolution. EU under separate 15% tariff ceiling; EU-Canada trade linkage adds modest contagion risk to EUR crosses in a CAD shock scenario.
implications.AUD: Indirect risk-off commodity bloc contagion if CAD volatility spills broadly on Aug 21. AUDCAD may spike on the binary outcome.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol spike risk around Aug 21 close.

themes.watchLevel: Aug 21 end-of-day is the new hard binary — 48 hours away. Three scenarios: (1) Deal announced by Aug 21 = CAD relief 100-150 pips from pre-Aug 19 levels, retire theme — now elevated-probability given 'substantial progress' per Carney Aug 18 statement; (2) Further delay/extension = CAD relief 30-50 pips, theme extends to 'extended negotiation,' probability lower given the explicit Aug 21 language; (3) Tariffs land Aug 21 = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, Canada retaliation activates. 1.4080 remains key USDCAD technical ceiling — a reclaim signals tariff-risk re-pricing. USDCAD support at 1.3850-1.3900 on deal/delay relief. Section 338's permanent statutory nature means theme does not auto-expire even if a deal is struck until the proclamations are explicitly revoked.

themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime — USDJPY 159 consolidation, BOJ Sep hike odds ~80%, Japan CPI Aug 21 is next hard catalyst
themes.summary: As of August 19, the intervention regime is in a consolidation phase with USDJPY trading in a tight 158.60-159.50 range. On August 17, USDJPY sat at 159.10, having retraced roughly half of the gains achieved from the initial joint intervention low of ~155.20 reached on August 3. No follow-up intervention has landed in over two weeks since the initial Jul 30-Aug 3 joint US-Japan action — a gap that continues to allow carry traders to rebuild short-JPY positions. The BOJ September hike case has materially strengthened since the Aug 16 update. Japan Q2 GDP (preliminary) was released August 17 in line with consensus at 0.5% QoQ, confirming the economy is operating above its potential growth rate and providing the BOJ with the growth backdrop it needs to hike. MUFG Research (August 17) now marks the market as pricing approximately 80% probability of a BOJ rate hike in September, up from about 65% as of August 7 — a material re-pricing. MUFG's baseline projects the BOJ to raise the policy rate to 1.25% in September 2026, then 1.50% in January 2027, and 1.75% in June 2027. The next and most critical near-term catalyst is Japan national CPI, releasing August 21. ING projects headline CPI at 2.0% YoY and core at 1.8% YoY — a return of headline inflation to the BOJ's 2% target for the first time in recent months, driven by persistent import price pressures. A print in line with or above consensus would cement the September hike case at BOJ's Sep 17-18 meeting. The BOJ kept its short-term policy rate at 1.0% at its July meeting (8-1, Takata dissented for an immediate hike to 1.25%), with the board warning underlying inflation could exceed the 2% target and the BOJ raising its FY2026 GDP projection to 0.6% from 0.5%. The structural backdrop is unchanged: BOJ at 1.0% vs Fed at 3.5-3.75%, wide rate differential; the MUFG baseline sees Fed cuts in late 2026 narrowing the differential from both sides; yen short positioning remains elevated; JGB 10-year yield near 2.8% (30-year high) adding fiscal pressure. The July trade statistics release August 20 — whether the trade deficit expands or contracts amid ongoing yen depreciation is an additional data point for the medium-term currency direction.

implications.JPY: MAXIMUM tailwind from three converging forces: (1) G2 intervention with Bessent re-entry warning nominally active; (2) BOJ Sep hike probability now ~80% per MUFG market pricing; (3) Fed Sep hike odds reduced by data miss trifecta, narrowing differential from both sides. Counter-risk: USDJPY at 159+ with no follow-up intervention for 16+ days allows carry rebuild. If 160 breaks on a daily close without official response, regime credibility damage will be severe. Japan CPI Aug 21 (same day as Canada Section 338 new deadline) — beat reinforces September BOJ hike and is JPY-supportive; miss pushes hike to October, USDJPY lifts toward 160.
implications.USD: BOJ intervention chatter actively depressing broad DXY; USDJPY topside capped by intervention threat. Fed Sep hike odds ~40% on MUFG view, with 'room to keep policy on hold at September meeting' per MUFG (Aug 17). USDJPY most vulnerable into BOJ Sep 17-18 and Jackson Hole Aug 28.
implications.EUR: EUR/JPY sold by intervention mechanism. EUR/USD at upper 1.15s on BOJ intervention chatter per FXStreet. ECB at 2.40% vs Fed at 3.75%. Watch for reversal if intervention chatter fades without follow-through.
implications.GBP: GBP/JPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure. GBP/USD near 1.34-1.356 — new 3-month peaks per FXStreet. BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR. Two-way risk into Jackson Hole.
implications.CHF: CHF/JPY lower on intervention pressure. USDCHF under pressure from broad USD softness. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower; CAD FX dominated by Section 338 binary above all else. USD softness partially compresses USDCAD.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention pressure. AUDUSD on four-week winning streak per FOREX.com. Watch AUDJPY 93-95 range.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention pressure; NZDUSD benefits from USD softness.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is the immediate critical level — a daily close above 160 without official verbal or actual intervention signals carry traders overpowering the regime and constitutes a credibility break. USDJPY below 157.50 = intervention credibility reasserting. USDJPY below 155.20 (post-intervention low Aug 3) = regime decisively winning. Japan CPI Aug 21 — headline at or above 2.0% YoY per ING projection = cements Sep BOJ hike (~80% already priced); sub-1.8% core = hike risk shifts to October, USDJPY lifts toward 160. Japan July trade statistics Aug 20 — deficit expansion = JPY headwind; surprise surplus = JPY supportive. BOJ Sep 17-18 meeting is the live hard binary: hike to 1.25% = fundamental JPY support materialises, reduces intervention burden significantly; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 160+ re-test. Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (Warsh keynote Aug 28) — dovish USD framing extends JPY-positive environment; hawkish framing partially restores rate differential drag on JPY. FOMC minutes today Aug 19 2pm ET — hawkish tone restores some USD carry bid and is a near-term USDJPY upside risk. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately. JGB 10-year yield at 2.8% — if approaches 3.0%, BOJ forced to defend bonds vs yen simultaneously.

themes.title: Warsh Fed — FOMC minutes today, Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (8 days) is dominant USD binary, Sep hike odds ~40% but MUFG sees hold
themes.summary: The Jackson Hole symposium is now 8 days away and remains the dominant USD binary event on the macro calendar. The symposium runs August 27-29, with Warsh delivering the keynote on Friday morning August 28 — his first ever Jackson Hole address as Fed Chair. The theme is 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,' with roughly 120 central bankers and officials from more than 70 countries attending. A critical new near-term catalyst materialises today: the FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting release at 2:00pm ET on August 19. The minutes will be the first detailed window into how many FOMC members are actively pushing for a September hike and whether the three July dissenters who favoured hikes (per prior reporting) represent a growing or contained faction. MUFG Research (Aug 17) concluded that the July CPI data (+0.1% MoM, +3.4% YoY, in line) and flat PPI (0.0% vs 0.2% consensus) together give 'not only Fed Chair Kevin Warsh but also the more hawkish FOMC members the room they need to keep policy on hold at the September meeting' — a meaningful shift toward an implied hold. Meanwhile, analysts at InvestingLive (Aug 17) note that Warsh's track record since May — curtailed forward guidance, shortened post-meeting statements, evasive press conferences — argues against Warsh using Jackson Hole for explicit rate-path signalling, with the real signal potentially coming from committee dissent rather than the podium. The structural tension remains: at Warsh's first meeting in June, roughly half the FOMC penciled in 2026 rate hikes at his first meeting; three presidents dissented in favour of hikes at his second meeting in July. Warsh told reporters after July 29 that his Jackson Hole remarks would aim to frame 'big picture questions' rather than offer near-term guidance, and stated the Fed is 'not constrained by market prices.' The data backdrop entering JH: July CPI +0.1% MoM / +3.4% YoY (in-line, Aug 12), July PPI flat 0.0% vs 0.2% consensus (Aug 14), NFP -23K vs +80K (Aug 7) — all three pushing against a September hike. Sep hike odds remain near 40%. Nvidia reports the evening of August 26, placing the market's biggest earnings event 36 hours before the biggest Fed event — risk-on/risk-off equity dynamics may amplify FX moves around JH. EUR/USD at upper 1.15s; GBP/USD near new 3-month peaks around 1.3560 per FXStreet. July PCE also releases August 27, the morning Jackson Hole opens. Sep 11 CPI (August) is the next major data event post-JH. Sep FOMC Sep 16 is the hard policy event, 19 days after Warsh's keynote.

implications.USD: TWO-STEP BINARY: (1) Today Aug 19 FOMC minutes 2pm ET — hawkish tone (many members still favour Sep hike, inflation fight incomplete) restores some USD carry bid 30-50 pips near-term; dovish/divided tone extends USD weakness; (2) Jackson Hole Aug 28 — hawkish Warsh framing (Sep hike still on table) restores USD carry bid 100-150 pips across EUR/USD, GBP/USD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD; dovish or structural/framework framing (avoids rate-path, focuses on financial innovation theme) = EUR/USD retests 1.17+, DXY toward 98-99. Near-term: broad USD under pressure from data miss trifecta (NFP + CPI + PPI). MUFG baseline now sees Fed holding in September.
implications.JPY: Rate differential headwind from Warsh narrative significantly reduced by NFP + CPI + PPI data miss trio. Dovish JH + FOMC minutes = USDJPY three-pillar bearish case (intervention + fading Fed + live BOJ hike) reinforced. Hawkish JH = rate differential widens modestly but intervention credibility still caps topside near 160.
implications.EUR: EUR/USD at upper 1.15s. ECB at 2.40% vs Fed at 3.75%. Warsh dovish at JH = EUR/USD retests 1.17-1.19 range; Warsh hawkish = EUR/USD pulls back toward 1.1280. Watch for Nvidia-driven risk-on EUR spillover on Aug 26. July PCE on Aug 27 (JH open day) is a pre-keynote data risk.
implications.GBP: GBP/USD near 3-month peaks around 1.3560 — two-way risk into JH. BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR. JH binary drives near-term direction. FOMC minutes today are a near-term directional catalyst.
implications.CAD: USD softness provides USDCAD compressing tailwind but Section 338 binary on Aug 21 supersedes this narrative entirely for USDCAD this week. Post-Aug 21, Fed theme reasserts if Section 338 is resolved.
implications.AUD: RBA on hold with easing bias. AUDUSD on four-week winning streak; supported by USD softness. Watch 0.6500-0.6650 range into JH.
implications.NZD: RBNZ same dynamic as RBA. NZDUSD benefits from broad USD softness into JH.
implications.CHF: SNB in easing mode; USDCHF under pressure. CHF safe-haven bid in risk-off episodes around JH volatility.

themes.watchLevel: FOMC minutes today Aug 19 2pm ET — immediate near-term USD catalyst; hawkish tone (multiple members actively pushing Sep hike) = 30-50 pip USD bid; dovish/divided = extends USD weakness. Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 — Warsh keynote Fri Aug 28 morning is primary binary: hawkish (Sep hike still on table) restores USD carry bid 100-150 pips across board; dovish or framework speech extends USD weakness toward Q3 upper targets. Sep hike odds currently ~40% — MUFG baseline now sees hold; a drop below 25% or rise above 65% before JH would be a major intra-period mover. July PCE Aug 27 (JH opening morning) is a pre-keynote data risk. Nvidia earnings Aug 26 evening — risk-on equity spike may amplify USD weakness into JH open. Sep FOMC Sep 16 is the hard policy event (19 days post-JH). Sep 11 CPI (August) is next major data event post-JH. Sub-3.0% CPI reading = dovish tolerance materialises, hawkish theme ends. DXY closing and sustaining below 99.00 = market rejecting hawkish read entirely. EUR/USD sustained above 1.1600 pre-JH = market pricing in dovish JH outcome.
